blocks.h2: Why Skokie Buyers Scope the Sewer
blocks.body: Most Skokie homes were built in the 1940s, '50s and '60s, and many still drain through their original clay lateral. A standard home inspection doesn't look inside that pipe. A camera inspection during your inspection period shows roots, cracks and sags, with the location and depth of each. If a repair is needed, you'll know before closing, when it can still be part of the conversation.

blocks.h2: Sewer Camera Questions From Skokie Homeowners

items.q: Is a camera inspection worth it before buying in Skokie?
items.preview: Yes. Most laterals here are 60+ years old.
items.answer: Yes. Most Skokie laterals are 60 years old or more, and a standard home inspection doesn't look inside them.

items.q: Can the camera see under the basement floor?
items.answer: Yes. From the cleanout, the camera follows the line under the floor and out to the street.

items.preview: Accurate enough to plan a repair.
items.answer: Our locator picks up the camera's signal from above and marks the spot and the depth, so repairs can be planned precisely.

items.q: Can I share the video with the seller?
items.answer: Yes. You keep the recording to share with a seller, an agent or another contractor.

items.q: Can you inspect my line after a storm backup?
items.answer: Yes. It shows whether your line was blocked or the sewer system was full.

items.q: Can you scope the line on short notice?
items.answer: Usually within a few days, to fit your inspection window.

items.q: How much does a sewer camera inspection cost in Skokie?
items.preview: It depends on access and length. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on access and the length of the line. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
